IBM.rationale: IBM presents a mixed but slightly positive fundamental picture. On the positive side, the company has executed a successful pivot toward higher-margin software (11% YoY growth in Q1 2026), benefits from a z17 mainframe super-cycle (hardware +51% YoY), and has a $12.5B generative AI bookings pipeline. YoY fundamentals are solid: revenue +9.5%, EPS +14.3%, net income +15.3%, and operating cash flow +18.3% in Q1 2026. ROE is strong at 32.5% and gross margins are healthy at 58.4%. However, QoQ trends are concerning with revenue -6.2% and EPS -44.6% (though Q2 2025 was likely a seasonal peak). The stock has already re-rated significantly from its April lows (+19.1% in Q2), and the current P/E of 25.6x sits near the middle of its 19-51x range over the past year, suggesting fair rather than cheap valuation. Key risks include consulting segment sluggishness (1% growth), elevated debt ($57.7B per web sources), and management's conservative FY2026 guidance of 'above 5%' growth which disappointed the market. The upcoming Q2 2026 earnings (late July) could serve as a near-term catalyst if software acceleration continues, but the stock's recent run-up and fair valuation limit upside. Net-net: solid franchise with improving trajectory, but largely priced in at current levels.
